I could not derive this rigorously, so the answer below is an estimate.

The category \(\mathcal C\) is the Haagerup–Izumi category for \(G=\mathbb Z/5\), since \(d^2=5d+1\) with \(d=(5+\sqrt{29})/2\). Its Drinfeld center \(\mathcal B\) has global dimension \((5(1+d^2))^2\). The count asked for depends on the simple objects of \(\mathcal B\) with dimension \(1+d^2\) and on how a ribbon equivalence \(F:\mathcal B^\tau\to\mathcal B\) permutes them. I did not determine that set, its size, or how \(\tau\) acts on it.

The heuristic I used: \(\tau\) flips the sign of \(u=\sqrt{d+9}\), which plausibly swaps a pair of dimension-\((1+d^2)\) simples whose S-matrix entries differ by the sign of \(u\). Under that assumption, any ribbon equivalence must move both objects, giving \(m(F)=2\) for every \(F\). I have not verified that the set has exactly two elements, that \(\tau\) swaps them, or that a ribbon equivalence exists at all. If \(\mathcal B^\tau\) were not ribbon equivalent to \(\mathcal B\), the answer would instead be \(+\infty\).

ANSWER: 2
